journal: J. Am. Chem. Soc. 51(2), 323-337 (Heat Capacities in Aqueous Salt Solutions, by Merle Randall and Frederick D. Rossini)
experimental_method: Differential adiabatic-type heat capacity calorimetry: two flasks (Unit 1 water, Unit 2 solution) heated with electrical energy, temperature rise compared with multi-junction thermels (galvanometer); salt added stepwise to Unit 2 to get change in heat capacity.
uncertainties_stated: Average error in a given dCp measurement about 0.10 cal for all runs, 0.06 cal for sodium chloride; error in Phi at the smallest m (0.043) about 23 times that in dCp.
quality_remarks: Only NaCl raw data are tabulated (Table VI); data for the other nine salts (including Na2SO4, KCl, K2SO4) exist only as plots and rounded values (Table VII) and a thesis. Phi is derived from measured dt2. Temperature scale and pressure not stated. PDF is 23 pages and extends beyond this article (an article ending Received August 8, 1928, Published February 5, 1929 follows); only Table VI on pdf page 11 used.
not_extracted_tables: Table III (condensed log of Run 19): calibration run of Unit 2
Table IV (change in heat capacity of Unit 2 with volume): apparatus
Table V (condensed log of Run 64): single raw run log
Table VII (rounded values of Phi, partial molal Cp of solute and water, specific heat for NaCl, NaBr, NaI, NaNO3, Na2SO4, KCl, KBr, KI, KNO3, K2SO4): smoothed/derived from plots
Table VIII, IX, X: limiting values and slopes, derived
